events.stem:
Consider the following reactions. In each, look at the product that contains the named element (balanced equations are not needed).
(i) AsCl₃, H₂O  →  product containing As
(ii) Na₂B₄O₇, Borax, HF, H₂SO₄, heating  →  product containing B
(iii) CuCl₂, Cl⁻ (conc.), excess chloride  →  product containing Cu
(iv) N₂, H₂, Fe catalyst, 200 atm, 400-450°C  →  product containing N
(v) B₂H₆, H₂O, hydrolysis  →  product containing B
The number of reactions in which the named element in that product is sp² hybridised is
Give the answer as an integer.

members.working:
Identify product containing named element for each reaction:
(i) AsCl3 + H2O → AsO3H3 (arsenic oxyacid), As likely tetrahedral (sp3).
(ii) Borax (Na2B4O7) with HF, H2SO4, heating → likely B(OH)3 or B4O7? Boron in borax is in B-O network, but product containing B after reaction likely B(OH)3 (sp3).
(iii) CuCl2 + excess Cl- → CuCl2 (solid) or CuCl2·2H2O; Cu2+ typically sp3 hybridised in tetrahedral complexes.
(iv) N2 + H2 with Fe catalyst at high T/P → ammonia NH3 (sp3 hybridised N).
(v) B2H6 hydrolysis → B(OH)3 (sp3). None of these products involve planar, unsaturated hybridisation (sp2). All are typical tetrahedral or trigonal planar? CuCl2 may form linear? Cu(II) often square planar (dsp2) but not pure sp2. The question asks specifically sp2 hybridised; none are purely sp2. Thus count = 0.
Thus answer integer 0.

members.name: glm-5.3-flash
members.working: (i) AsCl₃ + H₂O → H₃AsO₃ (arsenious acid): As has a lone pair, pyramidal, sp³ — not sp². (ii) Borax + HF/H₂SO₄ → BF₃ (or HBF₄; the simple product BF₃): B is trigonal planar, sp² — counts. (iii) CuCl₂ in excess Cl⁻ → [CuCl₄]²⁻: Cu is tetrahedral sp³ — not sp². (iv) N₂ + H₂ (Haber) → NH₃: N is pyramidal sp³ — not sp². (v) B₂H₆ + H₂O → H₃BO₃ (boric acid): B is trigonal planar, sp² — counts. Total sp² = 2.
